$comment: Self-derived finetype drift contract for census/naics_2022, checked by the in-engine finetype_validate@1 gate (the model-free `ft_validate` DuckDB table macro). ft_validate MELTS every column to VARCHAR, so this contract uses ONLY the string-surviving JSON-Schema keywords. ENFORCED: the `pattern` on code, code_display and parent_code, finetype's canonical `identity.industry.naics` pattern narrowed to the sectors NAICS 2022 has (42 and 92, where the canonical pattern admits 41 and 91 as well), so every value it admits the canonical pattern the descriptor publishes admits too; its hyphenated branch is an exhaustive alternation of Census's three sector ranges (31-33, 44-45, 48-49), so no other range can wear that shape; the patterns on the ancestor codes, each at its own level's width; the closed `enum` on level, release and text_source; and `minLength`/`maxLength` envelopes on the text. NOT ENFORCED, by design: numeric ranges (a numeric `type` BACKFIRES to 100% reject once melted to VARCHAR, so depth carries none); NULLs (invisible to ft_validate); and object-level `required` (documentation only); scripts/check_code_list.py, the `check_code_list` step, refuses a NULL code, description or release and a parent or depth that breaks the ladder. Free-text fields carry LOOSE length envelopes with headroom. Derived from build/stage/naics.parquet on Census's workbook of 2026-11-18 (2,125 rows; the longest title 118 characters, description_full 400, definition 7,475): a pass-through on today's rows, a fail-closed tripwire for future drift (an unknown level, a malformed code, a release other than the edition).
